For the geometric data convention, orient $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ by the ordered dimensionless coordinates $(\theta^1,\theta^2,\theta^3)$; the corresponding length-coordinate frame $(\partial_{X^1},\partial_{X^2},\partial_{X^3})$ has the same orientation.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] and [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]; no use of the full Axiom of Choice is made here. Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, its normalized measure, the componentwise real Sobolev spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, and their weak-derivative and Fourier-coefficient conventions be exactly those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. In particular, $H^s$ is defined for integer $s\ge0$, the weak-derivative norm is equivalent to the Fourier-weight norm by [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]], and the trigonometric characters are a complete orthonormal system by [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]. A field is a function with the domain and codomain declaration of [[def-function]]; Sobolev fields are its $L^2$-equivalence classes, not pointwise representatives.

For finite $m\ge1$, open $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, compact $K\subseteq O$, $R\ge0$, and integer $s\ge5$, define the bounded admissible initial-state class

$$\mathcal S_s(K,R):=\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ has its continuous representative valued in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\}.$$

The representative is unique because two continuous functions equal almost everywhere on the torus agree everywhere. For a smooth periodic first-order reduction of the electrovacuum equations, its specified finite list of real state components is identified with one such $\mathbb R^m$-valued function; the state-component convention is part of that reduction. In the geometric data convention below, the component arrays are specified separately. This is a definition of admissible function-space classes only; it asserts no existence result for a coupled Einstein-Maxwell reduction.

For the geometric data convention, write the dimensionless torus coordinate as $\theta^i\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and introduce a fixed length scale $L_0>0$ in metres. The corresponding length coordinates are $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi L_0}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L_0\mathbb Z)^3$; the Sobolev variable remains $\theta$, and $X$ is not a second name for a coordinate on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. The arrays $h_{ij}(\theta)$ and $K_{ij}(\theta)$ are the covariant metric and second-fundamental-form components in the length-coordinate frame $\partial_{X^i}$, with $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$ and $K_{ij}=K_{ji}$. Let $\mathsf e_A(h)$, $A=1,2,3$, be the positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame obtained by Gram-Schmidt from the ordered global frame $(\partial_{X^1},\partial_{X^2},\partial_{X^3})$. For spatial vectors $e,b$, the electromagnetic component arrays in this convention are $e_A:=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A:=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$; these are the orthonormal observer components used in the Einstein-Maxwell first-order reduction. The frame coefficients are smooth functions of the positive matrix $(h_{ij})$. If $h\in H^{s+1}$ has range in a compact subset of the positive-definite matrices, the composition supplier gives these coefficients in $H^{s+1}$; since $s\ge5$, the Sobolev-algebra supplier gives their products with coordinate vector components in $H^s$. The inverse frame matrix has the same property, so the coordinate and orthonormal component arrays describe the same $H^s$ vector fields.

Thus the data component spaces mean $(h_{ij})\in H^{s+1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^9)$ with values in symmetric positive matrices, $(K_{ij})\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^9)$ with values in symmetric matrices, and $(e_A),(b_A)\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^3)$. A smooth periodic first-order state also includes the specified component functions of that reduction and the first spatial metric derivatives; in the above length-coordinate convention $v_{kij}:=\partial_{X^k}h_{ij}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^k}h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ carry one inverse-length factor. For a fixed field scale $F_0>0$ in tesla, the dimensionless physical component arrays are $h_{ij}$, $L_0K_{ij}$, $L_0v_{kij}$, $e_A/F_0$, and $b_A/F_0$. Each fixed rescaling is invertible and preserves the finite-component Sobolev topology. These are component and unit conventions, not additional field equations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** For each integer $s\ge0$, an $H^s$ class
$u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ **takes values in a set
$E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when it has a continuous representative whose values
lie in $E$. Such a representative is unique, since continuous functions equal
almost everywhere on the torus agree everywhere. A map $u:J\to H^s$ with
$J\subseteq I$ takes values in $E$ when every class $u(t)$ does. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S_s(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$
When an item fixes $s$, it may abbreviate this class by $\mathcal S(K,R)$.

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$ be an integer and let $J\subseteq I$ be
an interval. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$.

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ be an integer and let $J\subseteq I$ be
an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$ using the continuous representatives from (c);
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, with coefficients evaluated using
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$. This condition requires each
   displayed product to define an $L^2$ class; it does not assert a global
   coefficient-composition bound depending only on $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$.

**(f) Initial data.** For an integer $s\ge5$, **initial data for $(\star)$ at
time $0$** are a class $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ whose values
lie in a compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^q)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{q-1})$ for every integer $q\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $q$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le q$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer, and let
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to the state class and coefficient family in [F1]–[F2]. Its hypotheses match term by term: the unknown has $m$ real components on the specified $2\pi$-periodic torus, the coefficients are smooth on the same open state domain, $A^\mu$ are symmetric, $A^0$ is positive definite, the data range in compact $K\Subset K'$, and the integer regularity is $s\ge5$. It gives the common interval, value range, solution regularity and bounds.

(Every solution in the stated Sobolev class is classical.) Let $v$ be any Sobolev solution on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Since $s\ge5$, the embedding [F6] with $q=s-1$ and $m=1$ applies, so $v$ and its first spatial derivatives have representatives continuous jointly in $(t,x)$; continuity in $t$ follows from $v\in C^0H^{s-1}$. On each compact time subinterval, the matrix $A^0(t,x,v(t,x))$ is uniformly invertible: it is positive definite and its arguments range over a compact subset of $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times K'$. Define the continuous function $P_v:=-(A^0(t,x,v))^{-1}\bigl(\sum_iA^i(t,x,v)\partial_i v+B(t,x,v)\bigr)$. The distributional equation and the a.e.-in-time $L^2$ equation in the Sobolev-solution definition imply $\partial_tv=P_v$ as a spacetime distribution. For every smooth spatial test function $\varphi$, the continuous scalar function $t\mapsto\int v(t,x)\varphi(x)\,d\mu(x)$ therefore has distributional derivative $\int P_v(t,x)\varphi(x)\,d\mu(x)$; the ordinary fundamental theorem of calculus gives $v(t)-v(t_0)=\int_{t_0}^tP_v(r)\,dr$ in $L^2$ for every $t,t_0$. Both sides have continuous spatial representatives, so this equality holds pointwise. Thus $v$ is $C^1$ in spacetime and solves $(\star)$ pointwise. Its original $L^\infty H^s$ and $L^\infty H^{s-1}$ time-derivative bounds make it a classical solution in the exact sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]].

Let $u,v$ be two Sobolev solutions in the class specified by the Statement with the same initial state. Their essential $H^s$ bounds extend to every time: for any $t$, choose times outside the exceptional null set converging to $t$; continuity in $H^{s-1}$ makes every finite Fourier partial sum of $N_s(u(t))^2$ the limit of the corresponding sums at those times, so it is bounded by the essential bound, and taking the supremum over finite subsets gives a finite $N_s(u(t))$. The two norm-equivalence bounds in [F7] then give a pointwise $H^s$ bound. The same argument applies to $v$. With $K'$ as the compact value set and a common finite radius $R_*$ for these pointwise bounds, step 1.2 and [F4] give $u=v$ on $(-T,T)$. The continuous-dependence estimate in [F4] is exactly the claimed $H^{s-1}$ statement for the solutions from 1.1.
When the initial state is smooth, [F5] applies to the same solution from 1.1 and preserves smoothness on that same interval. No new interval or coupled Einstein-Maxwell conclusion is inferred.

risk_review.notes: Read all four proof steps and all seven exact direct suppliers, including uniqueness/stability and smooth-persistence proofs. Existence matches the same compact K,Kprime, bound R, integer s>=5, open state domain, time interval containing zero, and AC_omega. C0 H^(s-1) embeds continuously into C1 in space; the PDE supplies a continuous time derivative, so the distributional integral identity upgrades every stated Sobolev solution to classical. Finite Fourier sums and lower-norm time continuity recover pointwise high-norm bounds from essential bounds. Compact time subintervals give uniform inverse matrices, and the uniqueness supplier applies on these subintervals with common compact state range and finite radii. For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. $O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $a<b$ and $c<d$. Suppose $g,h:[a,b]\times[c,d]\to\mathbb R$ are continuous and, for every fixed $t\in[c,d]$, the function $x\mapsto g(x,t)$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ with derivative $h(x,t)$. Define

$$G(x):=\int_c^d g(x,t)\,dt.$$

Then $G$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ as a function on that interval and

$$G'(x)=\int_c^d h(x,t)\,dt\qquad(x\in[a,b]).$$

At $a$ and $b$ the derivative is relative and one-sided. The derivative hypothesis is imposed only for interior parameter values; continuity of $h$ supplies its endpoint values.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^q)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{q-1})$ for every integer $q\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $q$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le q$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and

normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k\ge4$ be an integer and let
$u,v\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $|\gamma|\le k-2$ the weak derivative $D^\gamma u$ has a
continuous representative and
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|D^\gamma u(x)|\le C_k\|u\|_{H^k},$$
with $C_k$ depending only on $k$;

**(b)** the pointwise product $uv$ of the continuous representatives lies in
$H^k$ and
$$\|uv\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|u\|_{H^k}\,\|v\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** if $\varphi\in C^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and
$w\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, then $\varphi w\in H^k$ and
$$\|\varphi w\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|\varphi\|_{C^k}\,\|w\|_{H^k}.$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$ be an integer, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

citations.quote: $$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, use the dimensionless coordinate $\theta^i$ and length coordinate $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], for a fixed $L_0>0$. The arrays $h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ are the length-coordinate covariant components with $h_{ij}\in H^{s+1}$ and $K_{ij}\in H^s$. The Sobolev components of $e,b$ are $e_A=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$ in the canonical positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $\mathsf e_A$ specified there; thus $e_A,b_A\in H^s$. If $\mathsf e_A=E_A^i\partial_{X^i}$, their coordinate components are $e^i=E_A^i e_A$ and $b^i=E_A^i b_A$. The coefficients $E_A^i$ are smooth functions of the positive matrix $h_{ij}$; on the compact range of each such metric, [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] puts them in $H^{s+1}$ and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] makes the coordinate components $H^s$ as well.

For these representatives define the spatial connection coefficients by $\Gamma(h)^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_{X^i}h_{j\ell}+\partial_{X^j}h_{i\ell}-\partial_{X^\ell}h_{ij})$, with $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On coordinate vector components put $D_i e^j=\partial_{X^i}e^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}e^k$ and $D_i b^j=\partial_{X^i}b^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}b^k$; on the covariant tensor $K$ put $D_iK_{jk}=\partial_{X^i}K_{jk}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ij}K_{\ell k}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ik}K_{j\ell}$. Define $R(h)$ by $R^a{}_{bij}=\partial_{X^i}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jb}-\partial_{X^j}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ib}+\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ic}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{jb}-\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jc}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{ib}$, followed by the Ricci and scalar contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Sobolev embedding gives $h\in C^{s-1}$ and $K,e,b\in C^{s-2}$; the uniform positive lower eigenvalue makes $h^{-1}$ well defined, and the smooth-composition and algebra suppliers give $\Gamma(h)\in H^s$, $R(h)\in H^{s-1}$, and $D K,D e,D b\in H^{s-1}$. Since $s\ge5$, these constraint terms have continuous representatives, and their displayed equalities mean pointwise equality of those representatives. In the SI interpretation, $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, and the orthonormal components $e_A,b_A$ have units tesla; the factors $\kappa/\mu_0$ give matching units in the constraints. No numerical parameter values are assigned here.

Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b.$$

Then $Q_{ab}$ is symmetric and trace-free, and the SI-normalized stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}$ satisfies

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c.$$

In the source-free case $J=0$, $\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, put $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$, $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$, and $(e\times b)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}e_jb_k$. Then

$$T^{\rm EM}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\rm EM}(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-\frac{(e\times b)_i}{\mu_0}.$$

These are pointwise tensor identities. In the SI interpretation $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ have units tesla; no measurement or physical applicability claim is included.

Let $(g,F)$ be a smooth source-free electrovacuum solution of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] on a neighborhood of a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$. Then the induced tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ satisfies all four constraints in [[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]], namely the two Maxwell divergence constraints and

$$R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\operatorname{tr}_hK=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for each $t\in I$ there are
$\delta>0$ and a chart $(U,x)$ such that
$\gamma(I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta))\subseteq U$ and every coordinate of
$x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of
$I\cap(t-\delta,t+\delta)$ in the sense of
[[def-absolutely-continuous-function]]. This includes one-sided neighborhoods
at included endpoints. Equivalently, for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the coordinates of $x\circ\gamma$ are
absolutely continuous on $[a,b]$. The equivalence and independence of the
chart and smooth atlas are proved in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]
clause (a); continuity is part of both formulations.

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point: a
constant chart representative has derivative zero everywhere in its interior,
contradicting the full-measure nonzero-velocity requirement.

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ q\in J^+(p)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves and the relations $\le$, $\ll$, $I^{\pm}$, $J^{\pm}$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. All curves below are curves in
that sense.

**(a) Chronology and causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **chronological** when there is
no $p\in M$ with $p\ll p$, equivalently when there is no nonconstant future
timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. It is **causal**
when there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with
$\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$; a nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
is called a **closed causal curve**, and a closed future timelike curve is
called a **closed timelike curve**.

**(b) Strong causality.** $(M,g,N)$ is **strongly causal** when for every
$p\in M$ and every open set $U\subseteq M$ with $p\in U$ there is an open set
$V$ with $p\in V\subseteq U$ such that for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and all $a\le s<t\le b$ with $\gamma(s)\in V$ and
$\gamma(t)\in V$ one has $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V$. Thus no causal curve can
leave $V$ and later re-enter it; a set $V$ with this property for all causal
curves is called **causally convex for causal curves that meet it twice**.

**(c) Global hyperbolicity.** $(M,g,N)$ is **globally hyperbolic** when it is
strongly causal and for all $p,q\in M$ the **causal diamond**
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact in the subspace topology
([[def-compact-space]]).

**(d) Time functions.** A **time function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a function
$u:M\to\mathbb R$ which is continuous from the manifold topology to the usual topology of
$\mathbb R$: for every $p\in M$ and every open neighborhood $W$ of $u(p)$
there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ with $u(V)\subseteq W$
([[def-continuous-map-top]]). It also satisfies
$u(\gamma(a))<u(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve
$\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ that is not constant on $[a,b]$.

**(e) Temporal functions.** A **temporal function** on $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth
function $u:M\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]])
whose gradient is past-directed timelike: writing $du$ for its differential
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]) and $\nabla u$ for the vector field
with $g(\nabla u,X)=du(X)$ for every smooth vector field $X$, constructed from
the inverse metric of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], one
has
$$g(\nabla u,\nabla u)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad du(N)=g(\nabla u,N)>0 .$$
The first inequality says that the gradient is nowhere zero and timelike; the
second fixes it as past-directed for the chosen time orientation. No level set
of a temporal function is asserted here to be a hypersurface or to be
spacelike, and no relation between temporal functions and compactness is
asserted; those claims are proved separately where they are used.

**(f) Scope and conventions.** These are mathematical conditions on the
Lorentzian model. Different sources define global hyperbolicity by equivalent
but differently phrased conditions; this page fixes the formulation of (c)
and proves the implications it uses. In particular no equivalence between
global hyperbolicity and the existence of a Cauchy hypersurface is asserted
by this definition, and the physical reading of strong causality or global
hyperbolicity as predictability of a classical model is adopted only in the
framework postulates.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

The **Riemannian volume density** is $\mu_g=\sqrt{\det G_x}\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$ in coordinates.

The matrix is that of [[prop-coordinate-criterion-for-a-riemannian-metric]], so its determinant is positive and smooth. The density frames and their absolute-Jacobian law are [[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]. In dimension zero take the empty determinant to be one, giving weight one at every point, independently of orientation. The compatibility of these local formulas is proved in [[lem-the-riemannian-volume-density-is-coordinate-independent]].
The local Riemannian volume densities glue to a positive smooth density independent of coordinates.

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold and assume countable choice. For a smooth compactly supported function $f:M\to\mathbb R$, define $\int_M f\mu_g$ by the intrinsic smooth density integral. More generally every compactly supported signed smooth density $\sigma$ on $M$ has its existing intrinsic integral, independently of a Riemannian metric.

[[lem-the-riemannian-volume-density-is-coordinate-independent]] makes $f\mu_g$ a smooth compactly supported density. Apply [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]] and [[thm-density-integration-is-defined-without-an-orientation]]; [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited precisely at chart-partition selection. In a chart the summand is the integral of the partition-weighted coefficient $f\sqrt{\det G}$. On a zero-manifold it is the finite sum of scalar density values, and empty support gives zero. No orientation is required.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Compactly supported smooth density integration is independent of charts and partition, linear, local, nonnegative on nonnegative densities and strictly positive for a nonzero nonnegative density. It is invariant under every diffeomorphism, without choosing an orientation. The finite-parametrization formula holds under the hypotheses of [[prop-integration-of-top-forms-by-finite-parametrizations]], with orientation preservation omitted and absolute Jacobians used.

Let $A \subseteq \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ be **any** subset of the extended real
line ([[def-extended-reals]]) and write $A_{\mathbb{R}} := A \cap \mathbb{R}$.
Then $A$ has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound in
$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ ([[def-upper-bound]]), each unique, which we write
$\sup A$ and $\inf A$ with the ambient set always $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
Explicitly:

- $\sup A = +\infty$ if $+\infty \in A$, or if $A_{\mathbb{R}}$ is not bounded above in $\mathbb{R}$;
- $\sup A = -\infty$ if $+\infty \notin A$ and $A_{\mathbb{R}} = \emptyset$;
- $\sup A$ is the real supremum $\sup A_{\mathbb{R}}$ ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) if $+\infty \notin A$ and $A_{\mathbb{R}}$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{R}$;

and dually, with $-\infty$ and $+\infty$ exchanged and "above" replaced by
"below", for $\inf A$ ([[def-infimum]], [[thm-infimum-property]]).

**Agreement.** If $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and bounded above in
$\mathbb{R}$ ([[def-bounded-set]]) then $\sup A$ computed in
$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is the real number $\sup A$ of
[[def-complete-ordered-field]]; if $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and
bounded below then $\inf A$ computed in $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is the real
number $\inf A$ of [[thm-infimum-property]]. In particular the notation is
unambiguous on the sets for which the real supremum and infimum are defined, and
$\sup \emptyset = -\infty$, $\inf \emptyset = +\infty$ in
$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.

**No hypothesis is placed on $A$.** This is exactly what the real supremum cannot
do, and it is why every $\limsup$ statement on this page holds for every sequence
rather than for bounded ones only. It is also not a weakening of the discipline
this library keeps around suprema: the operation supplied here is a *different*
operation, taken in a *different* ordered set, and the agreement clause records
exactly where the two coincide.

derivations.claim: Clause (a) reuses the exact global definitions in [F1]. On each compact parameter segment, the finite subdivision in (d) has chart representatives that are C1 on the closed pieces, so their coordinate components are absolutely continuous. On chart overlaps the chain rule carries each one-sided tangent by the transition Jacobian and preserves its nonzero future-causal property; refinements preserve the class and the finitely many joins have measure zero. Thus every selected path belongs to the global almost-everywhere causal class. The escape quantifiers define a subset of U, whose relative boundary is defined even when the escape set is empty or all of U.

By the embedded three-dimensional slice-chart convention in (b), each p in H has a local defining function f with H={f=0} and df nonzero on H. Put w=g^{-1}(df,·). Nondegeneracy gives w nonzero and T_pH=w-perp. The radical of g restricted to T_pH is T_pH intersect (T_pH)-perp = w-perp intersect span(w), so it is nonzero exactly when g(w,w)=g^{-1}(df,df)=0. Replacing the defining function multiplies df on H by a nonzero scalar and leaves this criterion unchanged. The Killing equivalence is precisely [F2]; no field equation is used.

The spacelike condition makes $h$ positive definite. Under a section coordinate change with Jacobian $J$, $h'=J^ThJ$, so $\sqrt{\det h'}=|\det J|\sqrt{\det h}$. Thus [F3] makes every test integral in (c) intrinsic and finite. The test family contains the zero function, whose integral is zero, and every test density $\chi\mu_h$ is nonnegative, so every integral is nonnegative by [F5]. Its set of values is a subset of $\overline{\mathbb R}$ and therefore has an extended-real supremum by [F6]. On compact $S$, the constant test $1$ is allowed. For every other test, linearity and nonnegativity in [F5] give $\int_S\mu_h-\int_S\chi\mu_h=\int_S(1-\chi)\mu_h\ge0$; hence the supremum equals $\int_S\mu_h$. The same definition gives zero on the empty section without choosing an orientation. The norm of the specified stationary field is a smooth scalar, so the positive-norm set is open; continuity excludes positive and negative norm at its boundary, proving that boundary lies in its zero set. No converse is inferred.

At an approached added point, the C2 coefficients of the extension metric and their derivatives through order two are continuous. Nondegeneracy makes the inverse coefficients C2, so the Christoffel coefficients are C1 and curvature coefficients are continuous. Every polynomial complete curvature contraction defined in (e) is therefore continuous and finite at the point. Its values converge to that finite value along the specified sequence, or as t increases to 1 along the specified curve. On j(U) these scalars equal those of g because the embedding is isometric. They cannot be unbounded on either approach, proving the obstruction.

On $H_*$, $g(\xi,\xi)$ vanishes, so its differential annihilates $TH$. The nonzero covector $\xi^\flat$ also annihilates $TH$, which has codimension one; hence the differential is a unique scalar multiple of $\xi^\flat$. Locally choose a smooth transverse field $Z$ with $\xi^\flat(Z)\ne0$. Then $\kappa_H=-d(g(\xi,\xi))(Z)/(2\xi^\flat(Z))$ is smooth and independent of $Z$, proving existence, uniqueness and patching. Constant scaling multiplies the left side by $a^2$ and the covector by $a$, giving $a\kappa_H$. The required nonempty dense $H_*$ excludes the identically zero Killing field and any open portion with zero generator, while allowing bifurcation zeros in its closure. At zeros of $\xi$ this division is unavailable. If a smooth extension from an adjacent nonzero portion exists, its values at closure points are uniquely fixed by continuity; no existence or zeroth-law claim follows.

The positive rest metric and projection supplied by [F4] uniquely identify each spatial covector with a spatial vector. Integral curves are maps into the spacetime, a chart is a coordinate map, and a tetrad is a basis field; identifying spatial component lists with one of those objects is not licensed. All clauses therefore define intrinsic objects with their stated inputs and qualifications, without imposing a potential or changing a field equation.
